title: Imported Media Fetched Over Plaintext HTTP for Protocol-Relative URLs
summary:
### Impact
When importing content, Ghost can download externally hosted media and store copies on the site. Some media URLs were downloaded over plaintext HTTP even when the media host supports HTTPS.

An attacker able to intercept network traffic between the Ghost server and the media host could replace these files with content of their choice, which would then be stored and served by the site. Media downloading only happens when an Administrator imports content.

### Vulnerable versions
This vulnerability is present in Ghost from v5.70.0 up to v6.75.0.

### Patches
v6.76.0 contains a fix for this issue.

### How to update
For self-hosters using Docker, find [Docker's official Ghost image here](https://hub.docker.com/_/ghost). Updating a Docker-based Ghost instance [is documented here](https://docs.ghost.org/install/docker#updating-ghost). 

If your Ghost is a Ghost-CLI install see our documentation on [updating it to the latest version here](https://docs.ghost.org/update). 

### References
We thank [ka3n1x](https://github.com/ka3n1x) for disclosing this vulnerability responsibly.

### For more information
If you have any questions or comments about this advisory, email us at [security@ghost.org](mailto:security@ghost.org).
